group_min.note: Parks Canada lists seasonal access restrictions in Banff only for Bryant Creek/Allenby Pass, the Lake Minnewanka area trails and the Moraine Lake area trails; Lake Agnes is not among them (read 25 Oct 2026). Restrictions can be added at short notice.

age_band.note: 7.8 km and 495 m (effort_km 12.75) against the age gates of suitability.md 6.2: over the 6-7 ceiling (6 km, 350 m), inside the 8-9 ceiling (9 km, 500 m, 14).

suitability.kid_note: A steady climb from the Lake Louise shore past Mirror Lake to a seasonal tea house on Lake Agnes. The last stretch is a flight of steps beside a waterfall. Little Beehive and Big Beehive are side trips.

carrier_ok.note: 495 m of climb is over the carrying-adult ceiling of suitability.md 6.2 (8 km, 400 m).

stroller.note: A Moderate mountain trail with 495 m of climb; the page does not mention strollers.

wheelchair.note: A Moderate mountain trail with 495 m of climb; the page gives no accessibility detail.

distance_km.note: 3.9 km one way, so 7.8 km return.

loss_m.note: Loss on the way up, as Parks Canada states it.

exposure.note: A forest trail and steps to a lake basin; the Beehive side trips are not part of this record.

v.note: Avalanche terrain: Parks Canada says the teahouse hikes are not safe from November through mid-May
Parks Canada shuttle to the Lake Louise Lakeshore from the Park and Ride; a reservation is required (2026 dates).
Paid parking at the lakeshore in shuttle season; the lot often fills before sunrise. Parks Canada says not to hike to Lake Agnes in winter or spring (avalanche terrain, November to mid-May).

food.quote: open mid-May and close after Canadian Thanksgiving in mid-October
food.note: A privately run tea house at the lake.

navigation.note: A maintained Parks Canada trail with junctions to the Beehives; signage is not described on the page.

dogs.quote: Dogs are allowed on all trails in the summer unless otherwise specified in trail restrictions and closures.
dogs.note: No restriction was listed for the Lake Agnes Trail when read. The national-park rule is a leash at all times.

group_min.note: Alberta Parks gives a group size limit of 15 for this trail (a maximum); it states no minimum.

age_band.note: 7.8 km and 320 m (effort_km 11.0) against the age gates of suitability.md 6.2: over the 6-7 ceiling (6 km), inside the 8-9 ceiling (9 km, 500 m, 14).

suitability.kid_note: A long, steady climb through subalpine forest from the Upper Kananaskis Lake shore to a lake under the Sarrail headwall.

carrier_ok.note: 7.8 km and 320 m is inside the carrying-adult ceiling of suitability.md 6.2 (8 km, 400 m, effort 12).

stroller.note: A climbing forest trail; the OSM ways are tagged unpaved, with a short wooden section. The official page does not mention strollers.

distance_km.note: 3.9 km one way, so 7.8 km return. Alberta Parks counts from the Upper Lake Trail, which the route follows first.

conflicts.note: Computed from the OSM ways named Rawson Lake Trail (24836168, 181184079, 181184081), 2.47 km from the Rawson Lake Trailhead node 269822212 to the lake shore, doubled; Overpass run api-2026-10-25-data-d3a-overpass. It leaves out the Upper Lake Trail approach that the official figure includes.

gain_m.note: Alberta Parks gives both units; the metre figure is used.

surface.note: OSM tags surface=unpaved on the trail ways and surface=wood on a 168 m section; unpaved is recorded as dirt. The official page is silent.

adult_time_min.note: Estimate, not stated by Alberta Parks: Naismith's rule on the official 7.8 km and 320 m (5 km/h plus 1 h per 600 m of climb) gives 125 min, widened to 180 min for a stop at the lake.

exposure.note: Alberta Parks describes a forest climb to a lake.
